title: Rewrite request fallback telemetry context and async routing gate
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Problem: The current smart routing hot path mixes fallback orchestration state with request telemetry context. This results in noisy metrics, difficulty correlating fallbacks to decision inputs, and contention in the routing RPC path. Additionally, the routing gate that serializes async fallback attempts is brittle and adds tail latency when leases are briefly unavailable. Goal: Decouple per-request telemetry from fallback decision state, introduce a lightweight request->decision handshake for stable attribution, and replace the synchronous routing gate with an async, lease-aware admission controller to reduce tail latency and lock contention. This is a refactor-first, behaviour-preserving change: external APIs and policy semantics should remain the same unless a rollback is required.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: each fallback event contains stable request_id, route_version, and decision_reason fields that are verifiable in traces
Performance: p99 routing latency for 95th percentile tenant load improves or remains within +/-5% post-rollout
Reliability: fallback rate and successful failover behavior unchanged within statistical noise on canary traffic
Code: new async admission controller is unit- and integration-tested; old gate removed from hotpath
Observability: Grafana dashboard updated with new fallback attribution panels and rollback checks
tasks: Design handshake contract and small protobuf addition for request->decision (design doc link)
Implement RequestTelemetryContext struct and thread-safe propagation across coroutines
Introduce AsyncAdmissionController with lease cache and backpressure queue
Migrate fallback coordinator to use handshake; remove legacy global gate locks
Add unit tests for telemetry propagation, and integration tests for admission controller under contention
Open canary rollout PR and update rollout playbook with rollback conditions
Update dashboards and alerts; add telemetry migration compatibility layer for older agents
risks: Telemetry contract mismatch could cause gaps if rollout is not coordinated with downstream consumers
Admission controller bug could introduce queueing and increase tail latency if leases are mis-estimated
Edge-case: simultaneous region failover plus admission backpressure could amplify retries and increase cost
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated: start with 5% of canary traffic for non-critical tenants
Expand to 25% after 48h monitoring (no regression), then 75% after 72h
Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics
During each step run automated A/B checks comparing fallback attribution and p99 latency
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off to restore legacy gate behavior
If metrics degrade after rollback, revert runtime PR and re-open investigation
Notify on-call and owners and schedule hotfix if rollback flips do not eliminate regression
testing_notes: Unit tests cover telemetry propagation through coroutine boundaries and across rpc edges
Integration test simulates lease churn and verifies admission controller fairness and starvation-free dequeuing
Load test includes a synthetic traffic mix with 90% short requests and 10% long-running sessions to validate tail behavior
E2E smoke suite will run against canary cluster before each expansion step
